title: Introduce operational cost lens and invocation trace weave for cost RCA
author: Priya Raman
release_notes: Adds Cost Lifecycle Atlas dashboard, a sampled invocation trace-weave that attaches log excerpts to cost spikes, and tuned alert rules for cohorted token-cost drivers. Backwards-compatible telemetry tags; no runtime breaking changes.
description: Context: This PR adds an Operational Cost Lens that correlates per-invocation token-level economic breakdowns with phase timing and sampled logs to speed up RCA for cost regressions. Motivation: teams spend too long chasing whether spikes are kernel queue/backpressure, long prompts, or batching inefficiencies; surfacing lifecycle cost drivers and tying sampled logs simplifies investigation and reduces pager churn. What changed: 1) telemetry schema extensions (token_cost_phase, token_origin_hint, kernel_queue_ms) with backward-compatible tagging; 2) a trace-weave service that attaches compact sampled log excerpts to representative cost spike traces; 3) dashboards: Cost Lifecycle Atlas (multi-dim heatmap) and Invocation Weave panel for quick drilldowns; 4) alert tuning: cohorted cost-driver rules that shift from a global token-SLO to driver-weighted thresholds; 5) sampling policy: reservoir-based sampler with decay to keep cardinality and index pressure bounded; 6) metrics exposition: per-cohort token-cost histograms and phase timing sparklines. Linear/Jira: ENG-3456 / SUP-912. Rollout plan: staggered rollout to staging canaries, then production edge with monitoring of ingest delta and storage headroom. Backwards compatibility: consumers that do not emit new tags will continue to function; new tags are ignored by older readers. Guardrails: cardinality ceiling enforced via single-key hashing and per-tenant reservoir limits (keep indexed label cardinality <1000 labels/hour). Testing: unit tests for sampler, integration test for trace-weave and dashboard smoke, e2e replay with synthetic cost bursts. Operational notes: sample retention is short-lived by design to avoid storage buildup; long-term records are compact rollups. Checklist: - [x] schema migration with compatibility tests - [x] service implementation and endpoint contract - [x] dashboard JSON and panel docs - [x] sampling guardrails and stress tests - [x] unit/integration/e2e tests - [x] staging rollout and monitoring hooks Links: design doc https://linear.app/notes/ENG-3456-design, runbook https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/cost-lens Notable constraints: sampling decay uses IPC-based token to avoid thundering writes across instances; dashboard queries defer to pre-aggregated rollups when timeframe >24h. Security: no new PII collected; logs attached to traces are redacted by existing log-sanitizer. Migration complexity: low. This PR is intended to reduce MTTR for cost incidents and provide a low-cardinality, actionable surface for SREs and on-call engineers.
